summary: Reverse-path filtering on customer edge causing intermittent control-plane heartbeat drops and model artifact fetch failures
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent failures fetching model artifacts and sporadic control-plane heartbeat timeouts from serving nodes in their private deployment. Failures started after a network maintenance on the customer edge on 2025-11-06 and present as transient 5xx errors from artifact proxy and repeated gRPC CONNECT failures for control-plane health checks. Impact:
- Model downloads fail ~5-15% of requests for nodes in us-east availability zones, causing cold-start stalls and retry storms.
- Control-plane heartbeat drops cause short-lived routing fallback to secondary region for some requests.
Environment:
- Private deployment (VPC peering to Redwood control plane).
- Customer-managed on-prem egress via a NAT/edge router.
- NACLs in place with ephemeral port range 32768-61000 allowed.
Steps to reproduce:
1) Trigger model pull on a fresh serving node (force cold start).
2) Observe repeated fetch attempts in logs with TLS handshake errors or connection reset from remote side.
3) Correlate with control-plane heartbeat logs showing gRPC DEADLINE_EXCEEDED then recovery.
Observed behavior:
- TCP handshake completes intermittently but return packets are not reaching our control-plane IP, causing TLS read timeouts and gRPC reconnects.
- Packet captures provided by customer show SYN from node to control-plane IP, SYN/ACK returned, but subsequent ACKs not seen on node.
Expected behavior:
- Symmetric routing where return path reaches the originating node and TLS/gRPC sessions complete reliably.
Logs/traces provided:
- tcpdump from serving node (pcap snippet) showing SYN->SYN/ACK->no ACK from node side.
- Control-plane nginx/proxy logs showing established connections closed with short TCP timeouts.
- VPC flow logs showing control-plane source IP routed via peering, but return path observed leaving customer edge on different egress IP.
Workaround attempted by customer:
- Temporarily routed control-plane IPs through a dedicated NAT via a different egress; success rate improved.
- Disabled aggressive TCP connection reuse on their proxy; partial improvement.
comments: 2025-11-06 09:12 Asha Patel: Triage note - customer reports incident after edge maintenance. Asking for pcap, traceroute, and VPC flow logs. SLA P1 engaged.

2025-11-06 10:03 Customer (DataStream Health): Uploaded pcap and flow logs to shared S3. We see SYN/ACK from control-plane IP but our nodes never send ACK. Only happens for certain source-ports and at ~5-15% rate.

2025-11-06 13:20 Miguel Alvarez (SRE): Initial hypothesis - asymmetric routing / reverse-path filter on customer edge dropping return-path ACKs. Asked customer to run 'sysctl net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter' and provide edge router config.

2025-11-06 16:02 Customer: Edge router configured to strict rp_filter on the egress interface after maintenance. Provided router config snippet showing rp_filter=1 (strict) and new route-map changes for BGP introducing alternate egress for specific prefixes.

2025-11-07 09:45 Miguel Alvarez: Reproduced pattern in lab by creating asymmetric route on test VM and enabling strict rp_filter. Observed identical behavior: SYN/ACK received but strict rp_filter drops ACKs because return route would not match incoming interface.
resolution: In progress - customer applied temporary route pinning for control-plane prefixes to force symmetric egress and disabled strict rp_filter on their edge (set net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter=0) which immediately reduced failure rate to <0.5%. Next step is a coordinated change in customer's BGP policy to ensure symmetric paths and revert only after monitored stability. Recommended long-term: ensure route symmetry or set rp_filter to loose (2) and add specific static routes for control-plane and artifact distribution prefixes.
root_cause: Asymmetric egress introduced by recent edge BGP route-map change combined with strict reverse-path filtering on customer edge router. Return ACK packets for some ephemeral source ports were being dropped by rp_filter resulting in incomplete TCP/TLS handshakes and gRPC healthcheck failures.
next_steps: 1) Customer to implement BGP route policy to keep control-plane prefixes on single egress or add static routes for Redwood control-plane and artifact IP ranges. 2) If symmetric routing cannot be guaranteed, set rp_filter to 0 or 2 and add explicit static routes for control-plane prefixes. 3) Support to monitor for 48 hours and escalate to network partner if instability persists. 4) Postmortem and runbook update to include rp_filter checks during edge maintenance.
